title: Mass assignment on PATCH /api/users/:id to escalate role
user: Recon surfaced: PATCH /api/users/:id accepts a JSON body with user attributes. The authenticated user can update their own profile fields: {name, email, avatar_url}. The response includes a _role field (always 'user'). The backend appears to use Ruby on Rails 7.0.4 (from X-Powered-By header and JS manifest).
assistant:
RECON: PATCH /api/users/:id endpoint. The user can update name, email, avatar_url. The response includes _role which is always 'user'. Rails 7.0.4 has Active Record mass-assignment protection (strong parameters), but misconfiguration is common. The _role field in the response suggests the 'role' column exists in the users table.

HYPOTHESIS: Broken Object Property Level Authorization (OWASP API #5). The backend may accept a 'role' attribute in the request body even though it's not in the documented schema. If the strong parameters permit list is too broad (e.g., params.require(:user).permit!), adding "role":"admin" will be persisted.

TEST: minimum probe:
1. Send PATCH /api/users/{my_id} with body: {"name":"test","role":"admin"}.
2. Check the response _role field. If it's now 'admin', mass assignment is confirmed.
3. Alternative payloads to try: {"user":{"role":"admin"}} (wrapped), {"admin":true} (boolean column), {"is_admin":true}.
4. If the response doesn't reflect the change, try GET /api/users/{my_id} to check if the role was persisted.

INDICATOR: the response _role field changes to 'admin' after the PATCH, or subsequent API calls now return admin-level data.

Chainability: role escalation → admin API access → list all users → enumerate IDs → IDOR on all user data.
